purpose: Batch short selected-layer KV transfers into bounded request-owned GPU arenas
change: Opt-in kv_d2h_batch_tokens > 1 requires a positive max_device_bytes budget covering every slot and selected K/V component, including alignment.
Short KV ranges gather immediately into a private device arena; full batches and sealed tails copy to registered Host tensors. Large ranges bypass staging.
Cross-stream arena reuse is ordered; final completion fences earlier capture streams. Abort discards unpublished tails, and uncertain completion quarantines both Host and device storage.
Host tensor layout, raw teacher values, selected layers, immutable Store protocol and training alignment remain unchanged.
Server statistics and Prometheus expose allocated staging tensor bytes and the configured budget.

unit.scope: All test/registered/unit/training_capture tests, including direct and staged coordinator lifecycles. The expanded fourth CUDA case and stronger storage-retention assertion are covered by separate runs below.

report.scope: Profiler-only scopes; probes wait for capture slots. GPU work attribution, not serving latency or throughput.

checks.benchmark_invariants: All selected requests admitted and READY; same KV/aux payload bytes as native-index baseline; no quarantine, Catalog errors or cached prompt tokens.

limits: One H100, Qwen3-0.6B BF16, TP=1, local TCP Store and HTTP test Catalog; no cross-node RDMA evidence.
The byte budget covers staging tensor storage, not total CUDA allocator reservations, model KV, raw teacher computation or transient large-prefill gathers.
Profiler probes wait for capture reservations and run at 100% selection; their summed CPU/GPU work is not normal-serving wall time.
KV gather kernels and teacher/position D2H still execute per forward; reducing KV DMA calls does not eliminate capture overhead.
Two synthetic serving rounds with the same seed do not establish statistical significance, representative production performance or a service SLO.
New metric values have unit coverage and device allocation is observed in real server statistics; Grafana runtime acceptance is still pending.
Production SpecForge Catalog/consumer, trained draft quality, TP/PP/PD and non-static speculative deployment remain open.

scope.workload: seeded fixed-length random-ids, closed-loop concurrency, not production traffic
scope.timing: Client timing excludes warmup, server launch, readback and post-response writer drain
scope.payload_bytes: Validated manifest tensor sizes; not D2H or wire byte counters

benchmark.interpretation: KV batching removes most small KV DMA calls. Normal-serving output throughput is 0.8%/1.7% higher than the prior native-index capture phases, with 15.5%/16.3% loss against each new round's off baseline. Two rounds do not establish significance or meet a production SLO.
